android_mechanism: Network resource (socket/stream) not released after use; fix closes/releases it
bug_description: getWeatherUtil.getWeather creates a new http.createHttp() session for every weather request but never calls request.destroy(). Each city refresh leaks an HTTP session (connection and file descriptors) until GC finalization, so repeated refreshes and multi-city loads accumulate retained sockets/fds and slowly degrade networking.
fix_summary: The request session is destroyed in a finally handler after the response/error callback completes.
trigger_steps: Launch the app (it fetches weather for the default city list), then add several cities and switch between city tabs, triggering 30+ weather requests total.
Start hitrace capture (categories: app, sched, network, net) for the last 10 refreshes.
Record open-fd count of the app process before and after (hdc shell 'ls /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l').
Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install the fixed HAP and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: Growth of the app process fd count and ESTABLISHED/TIME_WAIT socket count attributable to weather requests after N refreshes.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed retains roughly one session (fd) per request after requests complete; fixed returns to baseline. unfixed_fd_growth > fixed_fd_growth by >= 5x over 30 requests.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 60 app sched network net -o /data/local/tmp/wa_leak.chtrace
